148 THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

Susan. The professor is an Odd Fellow and, with his wife, a member of the Christian Church.

Information for the activities of Professor Halsell for the next few years is incomplete. Professor R. C. Gee, who was his educational associate for a time, in an article in The Savoy Star,*  writes that Professor Halsell taught in Anson, Texas, for two years (1890-1892) and then returned to Savoy for two years, joining with Mr. Gee who was his educational associate for a time, continued to encourage Savoy College to Wichita Falls, or to Camp County, to continue his educational work there. The sketch from that period of his life has not yet been made, in Sherman, Texas.

On July 25, 1869, the professor Miss Annie College—whose maiden name was Leah Alls—and, Miss Maggie[?] Tones, of that place. With the pupils from both College of the State, the letter are based on the impress of the College upon them. To this happy union twelve children were born, all natives of the same State. *Personal letter from Miss Maggie Toms, Calera, Oklahoma, July 14, 1938.
